title: I turned Fellvault’s Mythic sword capture into a Godot regression test
author: Knuckleclot
selftext:
I’m building Fellvault, a dark fantasy idle RPG in Godot. I wanted to film a sword going from shards to a Keeper fight. The part I wanted to verify was that the weapon I saw in combat was the exact item I’d crafted, even after I changed screens and refined it.

I used Codex to write a GDScript capture harness around the existing UI handlers. The demo save starts with 270 matching shards. After pressing Craft, the script checks for one new Mythic Riftwrought Sword and 30 shards left. It keeps the new item’s UID, checks that Equip puts that UID in the weapon slot, confirms the battle rig shows Mythic, then refines the same item before calling Rift Strike in the Stage 625 Keeper encounter. The save is isolated and persistence is off for the capture.

The same harness runs headless for the checks and in a window to save frames. It also writes the craft, equip, refine and Fury frame numbers to JSON, which gave me reliable cut points for the short. The image shows the actual before-and-after weapon swap from that recording.

For devs testing in Godot, where do you draw the line between calling the same handlers as the UI and driving the whole flow with simulated input? I’m curious what you’ve found catches the most UI regressions.

[Playable desktop build on itch.io](https://fellvault.itch.io/fellvault) · [Fellvault site and mobile beta](https://fellvault-web.vercel.app/#beta)

Codex helped with the GDScript harness, tests, gameplay implementation and some text. Some in-game artwork uses generative AI.
